name: New reply in a thread
description: Delivers a reply in a discussion, with the comment it answers carried underneath it so the whole exchange reads in the inbox.

origin.note: Design: thread — the new reply first in full ink behind an accent rule, the comment it answers set back beneath it in a bar-marked card, two actions of unequal weight between them.

subject: New reply from {{ reply_author }}
preheader: The reply and the comment it answers are both here, so the thread reads without a login.

thread_title.description: What the discussion is called. Set as the eyebrow so a reader with four of these in their inbox can tell them apart before opening any of them.
thread_title.example: Deploy pipeline times out on large migrations

reply_text.description: The reply in full. Truncating it defeats the point of the email — the reader would have to open the app, which is the trip this message exists to save.
reply_text.example: It's the migration lock, not the pipeline. I raised the statement timeout to 300s on staging and the same job finished in four minutes.

reply_time.description: When the reply was posted, in the recipient's timezone if you know it. Attached to the quotation, because it dates the words rather than the delivery.

parent_label.description: The line that introduces the quoted parent. Two words, lower case, doing the job a threading indent does on screen.

parent_author.description: Who wrote the comment being answered. Often the recipient, which is exactly why it has to be named rather than assumed.

parent_text.description: The comment the reply answers. Leave it empty when the reply opens a thread and there is nothing to quote; the whole quoted block then disappears rather than showing an empty box.
parent_text.example: Anyone seen the importer hang at 40%? Third time this week on the same account.

reply_label.description: Label on the action that continues the conversation. This is the one the sender wants pressed, so it carries the filled button.

reply_url.description: Deep link that opens the composer on this thread, not the thread's top.

thread_label.description: Label on the quieter action, for people who want to read the rest before answering.

thread_url.description: The whole discussion, for the replies that did not make it into this email.

thread_meta.description: One closing line of provenance — how many people are in the thread, and why the recipient is one of them. It answers "why am I getting this" before the reader has to ask it.
thread_meta.example: 4 people in this thread. You are following it because you commented.

notification_settings_url.description: Where thread notifications get batched or switched off. A busy thread can send a dozen of these in an afternoon, so the escape has to be in every one of them.

notification_settings_label.description: Wording of that link. Offer less noise, not a settings screen.
notification_settings_label.default: Change how often you get these
